free_tier.stated: 5 GB of free storage for files in Microsoft Teams for personal use; images and videos are not saved on OneDrive and have no storage limit; attached files go to the Microsoft Teams Chat Files folder in the user's OneDrive
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Unmetered; share links resolve to OneDrive direct URLs.

tooling: Graph API chatMessageHostedContent + driveItem; no rclone backend for Teams specifically (use the onedrive remote pointing at the Chat Files folder)
chaining: Effectively OneDrive consumer's 5 GB wearing a different hat - Teams free files ARE OneDrive files, so this is not a second quota. The one genuine loophole claim on the page is 'Images and videos are not saved on OneDrive and don't have a storage limit' - unverified whether that means arbitrary files can be smuggled as media.
limits_note: 5 GB total files; 250 GB max individual file upload/download; chat messages unlimited.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: no signup identity requirement is stated on the storage page read; it only describes where personal-use data is stored

reliability_note: Leaving a community does not revoke other members' access; deleting the 5 GB block blocks attaches but not history.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.
